title: 4D Command IR — three-layer syntax schema
description: Layer 1: per-command signatures. Layer 2: shared substructures (enums, sub-grammars, protocols, handle types, callback contracts) referenced by pointer. Layer 3: relationships between command/overload entries.

enums.description: Layer 2 — named, reusable constant sets (e.g. Field and Variable Types). Referenced from parameters via {"kind":"enum_ref","enum":"<key>"}.

subGrammars.description: Layer 2 — 4D-native mini-grammars fully specifiable from 4D's own docs (e.g. dotted attribute paths with [] array markers). Referenced via {"kind":"subgrammar_ref","grammar":"<key>"}.

foreignGrammars.description: Layer 2 — external, non-4D grammars (SQL, regex, WSDL, JS, ...) that this corpus cannot itself fully specify. Referenced via {"kind":"foreign_grammar","grammar":"<key>"}.

protocols.description: Layer 2 — multi-statement or multi-command usage protocols that no single call's signature can express alone.

handleTypes.description: Layer 2 — opaque reference/handle types produced by some commands and consumed by others (DOM refs, SAX contexts, list refs, ...).

callbackContracts.description: Layer 2 — expected calling conventions for methods registered as callbacks (e.g. ON ERR CALL targets).

commands.description: Layer 1 — one entry per command, each with one or more overloads.

relationships.description: Layer 3 — edges between command/overload entries: supersession, mutual exclusion, near-duplicate deltas, structural equivalence, mechanism families, platform variants.

CommandRef.description: Pointer to a command, optionally scoped to a specific overload index (0-based).

rules.description: Plain-language grammar rules (e.g. dot-separates path segments; trailing [] marks an array attribute; optional letter inside [] names an element reference).

validatableByThisCorpus.description: Always false — flags that this corpus has no authority to check well-formedness of this grammar.

MultiCallChainProtocol.description: Category A — a command called repeatedly, each call contributing one unit, with a leading/trailing marker distinguishing 'more to come' from 'execute now'.

leadingDiscriminatorParam.description: Name of the optional leading param (e.g. conjOp) used to join this call to the previous one, if any.

continuationParam.description: Name of the trailing param (typically literal *) whose presence means 'more calls coming' and whose absence triggers execution.

StateMachineProtocol.description: Category L — a small grammar over a *family* of distinct named commands that must be called in a valid nested/ordered sequence (e.g. SAX open/set/close).

HandleTypeDef.description: Category M — produce/consume/destroy lifecycle for an opaque reference type.

CallbackContractDef.description: Category N — the implicit expected signature of a method registered as a callback, documented only in prose about the callback target, not in the registering command's own signature.

trigger.description: What causes 4D to invoke the registered method.

TypeRef.description: A single type reference. oneOf several kinds, covering concrete types, 4D's own catch-all pseudo-types, pointers whose target can't be resolved statically, literal-symbol sets, and pointers into the Layer 2 shared tables.

name.description: e.g. Text, Integer, Real, Boolean, Date, Time, Picture, Blob, Object, Collection, Table, Field, Array, Variable, or a 4D.<Class> OOP type.

oneOf.description: Category O — fake/catch-all types 4D uses because the real type varies by context or can't be pinned down.

possibleTargets.description: e.g. ["Table", "Field"] — what the pointer might reference; not distinguishable from the call site.

oneOf.description: Category S — statically indistinguishable overload targets.
Category D — value drawn from a shared, globally-referenced enum (e.g. Field and Variable Types constants).
Multi-type parameter, e.g. 'Text, Real, Date, Time'.

sentinelValues.description: Category H — reserved special values carved out of an otherwise-open type.

blocksOnOmission.description: Category E — omitting this parameter triggers a blocking interactive UI dialog rather than a default.

silentCoercionDefault.description: Category P — deterministic fallback conversion applied when this parameter's type can't be resolved (often across a language boundary).

elementTypeSelectsMode.description: Category G — for array-typed parameters where the element type (e.g. Integer vs Boolean) changes the whole call's semantics, not just coerces.

VariadicGroup.description: Category B — a named cluster of 1+ parameters that repeats as a unit within a single call.

ContentBindingPair.description: A matched pair: one param holds literal content, the other a live variable/pointer binding to the same content (e.g. headerName/headerVar).

OverloadElement.description: One slot in an overload's parameter list: a plain parameter, a variadic group, or a content/binding pair.

semanticRole.description: Category C (part 2) / general — short discriminator of what THIS overload does, distinct from sibling overloads even when types look similar.

mechanism.description: e.g. 'static_variadic', 'indirect_array_of_pointers', 'object_map_equivalent' — flags when two overloads solve the same problem via structurally different means (MULTI SORT ARRAY case).

discriminatedBy.description: How a caller/generator picks this overload vs siblings.

staticallyDistinguishable.description: Category S — set false when this overload cannot be told apart from a sibling by declared types alone.

jointConstraints.description: Category R — cross-parameter validation rules among named siblings, not expressible as independent per-param rules.

interactionNotes.description: Free-text notes on directional/partial overrides between named optional params (e.g. MODIFY SELECTION's two trailing *'s).

protocolRefs.description: Category A/L — keys into root.protocols.multiCallChains / .stateMachines that this command participates in.

handleRoles.description: Category M — which handle type(s) this command produces/consumes/destroys.

callbackContractRef.description: Category N — key into root.callbackContracts, if this command registers a callback.

externalSchemaSource.description: Category K — signature/valid-values are only fully knowable from an external artifact, not this doc.

constraints.description: Prose-derived rules not expressible as types (e.g. 'must specify aTable, cannot use default table').

gatedBy.description: e.g. a compatibility setting that must be enabled for the change to apply.
